raw_response:
I am 49 years old and have farmed these 7.8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I finished middle school. My family has six people, and my son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan city, so they send money home. That helps me buy seed and fertilizer, but I still watch every yuan because fertilizer prices went up again this year.

I put 6 mu into wheat-maize because that is the safe rotation everyone here does. The other 1.8 mu I plant cotton because last year Lao Zhang from the east side of the village got a good price for his cotton, and I want to keep some cotton in my mix.

For wheat, I sow in October with improved seed, 13 kg per mu. I buy it from the dealer in town. Last year I used 12 kg per mu and the stand was a bit thin, so this year I add 1 kg more. For fertilizer, I put one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Then at green-up I spread 20 kg urea per mu, and at jointing another 10 kg urea. That gives me about 17 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray pesticide twice. I use rotary tillage before sowing. Last year I got 480 kg per mu; this year I expect 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, after we cut wheat in June, I hire a machine to drill hybrid seed directly into the stubble, 2.5 kg per mu. No plowing — saves 80 yuan per mu and we are racing the clock before the summer rains end. I put 40 kg compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and if the leaves look light green at the big trumpet stage, I add 15 kg urea. That is about 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, once at jointing and once at filling if it does not rain. I spray pesticide twice. I expect 580 kg per mu.

For cotton, I plow the 1.8 mu in April because cotton likes loose soil. I use a hybrid seed, 1 kg per mu. Cotton needs more potassium, so I put one bag of compound fertilizer plus extra potassium fertilizer per mu as base. I topdress twice with urea during flowering. Total is about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Cotton drinks more water at flowering and boll stage, so I irrigate four times. I spray pesticide five times because bollworm always comes. I expect 280 kg seed cotton per mu.

I would rather spend more on fertilizer than risk yield. A bad harvest means no money for my grandson's school fees. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I accept. I watch what my neighbors do, and everyone around me uses about the same amounts. Change is risky, so I stick close to what I did last year, with small adjustments. My son's off-farm income gives me some room to invest, but I still balance the whole budget carefully.
